findings.title: Warming and wetland plants (2013)

findings.interpretation: Mostly held. In an Alaskan coastal wetland, warming raised graminoid biomass by 20% in the second summer. findings.original_claim: Fiscal sustainability and the accuracy of macroeconomic forecasts: Do supranational forecasts rather than government forecasts make a difference? — https://doi.org/10.1504/ijse.2011.039440
findings.interpretation: Held. The EU’s budgetary frameworks directive requires national forecasts to be compared with the Commission’s and large gaps explained. Later work finds optimistic growth forecasts still drive optimistic budgets, with high-profile fiscal councils helping, and that the Commission’s own fiscal forecasts turn more optimistic when a deficit threatens to breach 3%.

findings.title: UK food futures (2011)
findings.original_claim: Food futures: system transitions towards UK food security — https://doi.org/10.4337/jhre.2011.02.04
findings.interpretation: Partly. Shocks hit hard, with food inflation peaking at 19.1% in March 2023, the highest since 1977, yet overall UK production and trade stayed broadly stable. The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) calls the long-term decline of natural capital a pressing risk.

findings.title: Metrology research foresight (2011)
findings.original_claim: Foresight on the future of public research metrology in Europe — https://doi.org/10.1108/14636681111109660
findings.interpretation: Held. The European Metrology Programme for Innovation and Research (EMPIR) ran from 2014 with €600m and 240 projects, closing in 2026. Its successor, the European Partnership on Metrology, has €740m aimed at climate, digital and health challenges, including self-sustaining European metrology networks.

findings.title: POPs under climate change (2011)
findings.original_claim: Potential implications of future climate and land‐cover changes for the fate and distribution of persistent organic pollutants in Europe — https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2010.00547.x
findings.interpretation: Partly. The Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme (AMAP) found persistent organic pollutant levels tracking temperature, precipitation and sea ice, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Hexachlorobenzene (HCB) has been rising in the air at stations on Svalbard and Iceland. The evidence is mostly Arctic.

findings.title: Constructivist forecasting, EU as a military power (2011)
findings.original_claim: The Purpose and Pitfalls of Constructivist Forecasting: Insights from Strategic Culture Research for the European Union’s Evolution as a Military Power1 — https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-2478.2011.00648.x
findings.interpretation: Held. EU strategic cultures were converging even before the Ukraine war, which then boosted EU defence thinking (2026). ReArm Europe brought a roughly €800bn defence push (2025), and “strategic autonomy” became the EU’s key frame (2026).
